definition: A linked list stores each element in a node that points at the next node. The list itself holds only the first node, and reaching the element at position k takes k steps. Inserting or removing a node is constant time when you already hold the neighboring node.
details: There is no index access in constant time. Use a list when you splice nodes you already have, not when you need random access.
A singly linked list can only move forward.

complexity.time: Access by position is O(n). Insert or delete at a known node is O(1).
complexity.space: O(n) space for the elements themselves.

examples: A playlist where songs are spliced in without shifting later songs
A free list of reusable blocks inside an allocator
